mac_setup_notes: Hardware: Apple M5 Max, 64 GB unified memory, 2 TB SSD, macOS high-power mode on AC (methodology.md lines 45-50). Per apple.com MacBook Pro specs (https://www.apple.com/macbook-pro/specs/, fetched 2026-11-16), 64 GB is only offered with the 40-core-GPU M5 Max, which has 614 GB/s of memory bandwidth, so the measuring machine is a 614 GB/s part. This laptop's RTX 5080 has 896 GB/s, a decode ceiling about 1.46x higher for models that sit fully in VRAM (estimate). Engine: Ollama 0.32.13 and 0.33.0 on the OpenAI-compatible /v1 endpoint, not /api/chat (setup.md lines 26-34). The engine changes results: gemma4:12b investigate went from 5/5 on 0.32.13 to 1/5 on 0.33.0 with the same digest, and the four losses were turns spent thinking with no tool call (methodology.md lines 54-67). Ollama is at 0.40.16 now (Docker Hub tags 0.33.0, 0.32.13 and 0.40.16 all exist, checked 2026-11-16), so pass/fail on today's Ollama is not proven. Measured 22-23 August 2026. The tags were republished since then: today's GGUF manifests come from builds named 2026-09-27/29, and the tags page says the default tags were updated about a month ago. The bytes measured are therefore not the bytes a CUDA host pulls today. The Mac disk sizes (e4b 9.5 GB, 12b 7.6 GB, 26b 16 GB, 31b 19 GB) match today's MLX variants (e4b-mlx 9.5 GB, 12b-mlx 7.7 GB, 26b-nvfp4 16 GB, 31b-mlx 19 GB) better than the GGUF variants a Linux host gets (about 6.6, 8.0, 18.7 and 20.4 GB). The Mac may have run Ollama's MLX path, but that is unverified, because the docs do not record the digest or runner. Context: the docs do not record OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH or num_ctx. The workload is a short agent loop over a small SQLite schema, so it probably needed far less than OpenCode's 64k, and Ollama's default on a 64 GB Mac is large anyway (inferred). Sampling: Studio sends temperature 0 and top_p 1 to every model (measured-profiles.json measuredAgainst.defaults), not the Gemma card's 1.0/0.95/64. Ollama's params blob for these tags adds top_k 64, temperature 1, top_p 0.95 and draft_num_predict 3, and the request overrides only temperature and top_p. Per-turn limit: the shipped 90 s, with per-model overrides from src/lib/agent/model-tuning/measured-profiles.json. gemma4:e4b uses the defaults (90 s, nothing else). gemma4:12b uses 150 s, suppressAgentReasoning and suppressPlanReasoning (no thinking on any turn). gemma4:26b uses 90 s, unreportedCallCeiling 10 and retryEmptyTurn. gemma4:31b uses 150 s and suppressPlanReasoning. Thermal: a 3.5 h back-to-back sweep dropped gemma4:26b to 1/5 on one cell at 87-93 s per run, and it read 5/5 at 36 s on a rested machine. The published figures are rested-machine re-reads (methodology.md lines 80-90). Pass rule: 5 consecutive 'answered' verdicts per surface. The verifier checks that the model read, presented and cited, not that its SQL was correct. Durations are whole agent-run seconds (median of passing runs), not tok/s.

models.fit_detail: (estimate) Weights, projector and draft come to 7.47 GiB. Global KV f16 = 8 layers x 1 head x 512 x 2 (K,V) x 2 B = 16 KiB/token, so 1.0 GiB at 64k and 2.0 GiB at 128k. The sliding cache is about 0.32 GiB (40 x 8 x 256 x 4 B x 1024). Adding about 0.4 GiB CUDA context and 0.5-1 GiB compute gives about 9.7-10.2 GiB at 64k and 10.7-11.2 GiB at 128k against 15.47 GiB, so everything stays on the GPU even with f16 KV. 256k would be about 12.7-13.2 GiB and probably fits too. RAM need is only the page cache for the 7.5 GiB file.

models.reason: It is the fastest Gemma in the user's own harness, 30/30 with tool calls through Ollama /v1, and it fits fully in VRAM at 64k-128k with room to spare. The evidence is conditional on thinking being off on agent turns and on the engine version, and that condition has to carry over to OpenCode (thinking off by default, which also matches the KB's server-off rule). Its weak independent agentic scores (AA TB2.1 27.3) are the reason the KB keeps it below rank 10, and libredb does not test multi-line edit arguments.
models.opencode_suitability: Native tools and toggle thinking. Context up to 256k, and 64k-128k fits here. libredb evidence: reliable tool-call format and loop termination in short read-only loops (5 consecutive passes per surface), but only with reasoning suppressed. With thinking on it is bimodal: it either answers at once or thinks until the turn wall without calling a tool. In OpenCode, use the no-thinking variant by default. Untested by libredb: long contexts, file edits and multi-line streamed arguments (llama.cpp #29655 affects Gemma 4 edits).
models.speed_here_vs_mac: Faster or similar (estimate). The model fits fully in VRAM, so decode is bandwidth-bound and the ceiling rises by about 896/614 = 1.46x. Prefill on the RTX 5080 should also be at least as fast (estimate, unmeasured). The Mac's 11 s median is a whole-run figure that includes Studio overhead and tool latency, so expect roughly the same or somewhat shorter runs, not 1.46x across the board. A caveat: the Mac may have run the MLX variant, and this machine would run the GGUF Q4_K_M with MTP draft.

models.reason: It is already rank 5. The user's harness confirms it can complete tool loops reliably, but only with two libredb-specific guards: a lower call ceiling and an automatic retry of empty completions. Without the retry, assess lost 15 runs. That empty-completion-after-many-calls failure is the concrete risk to test in OpenCode, which (as far as the KB records) has no equivalent retry. Raw tool-call format is fine, but the model can stall with an empty turn deep in a loop. Combined with the KB's llama.cpp #29655 (multi-line streamed edit arguments), test both empty turns and multi-line edits in OpenCode before trusting it.
models.speed_here_vs_mac: It depends on the runtime (estimate). With llama.cpp QAT Q4_0 fully in VRAM, decode is faster than the Mac: about 2.4 GB of active weights per token gives a ceiling of about 375 tok/s here against about 230-250 tok/s at 614 GB/s, roughly 1.5x. With the Ollama default tag partly offloaded, about 30% of the active expert reads come from DDR5 (about 70-80 GB/s in practice of the 102.4 GB/s peak), giving a ceiling of roughly 60-80 tok/s, slower than the Mac. Whole-run seconds also depend on the empty-turn retries and thermal state, so do not transfer the 36 s median.

kb_implications: Gemma 4 12B (honorable mention): the user's own agent harness is first-hand evidence that it is the most reliable and fastest Gemma (30/30, 11 s median). The KB should add a 'tested by the user' line and an Ollama path next to the vLLM recipe: gemma4:12b (GGUF Q4_K_M plus draft, 7.47 GiB with the projector) fits all-in-VRAM at 64k-128k here (estimate). It should also record that this evidence holds only with thinking suppressed on every turn, and that it is engine-version sensitive (5/5 to 1/5 between Ollama 0.32.13 and 0.33.0). That supports the KB's rule to start toggle models with thinking off, and argues for testing Gemma 4 12B with thinking off in OpenCode before re-judging its rank.

Gemma 4 E4B: the KB excludes it for 'weak or missing agentic scores', but it passed the user's harness 30/30 with no tuning at all. The exclusion reason should be reworded to say that tool-call reliability is shown first-hand in short loops and that it is excluded for coding-agent quality and context-growth risk, not for tool failure. It could be listed as a sub-agent or tool-worker candidate (fits all-in-VRAM, about 8 GiB at 64k, estimate).

Gemma 4 26B-A4B (rank 5): confirmed as able to finish agent loops, but the user's evidence names a concrete failure mode the KB does not mention: an EMPTY completion (no call, no text) after about 11 tool calls, which cost 15 runs on one surface until an automatic empty-turn retry was added. Add this to the rank-5 caveats beside llama.cpp #29655, and add an 'empty turn deep in a tool loop' check to the OpenCode smoke tests.

Gemma 4 26B-A4B Ollama alternative: the KB says gemma4:26b-a4b-it-qat fits with 64k q8_0 KV. Recomputed against the measured 15.47 GiB, the 13.45 GiB model plus 1.11 GiB projector plus about 0.75 GiB KV plus CUDA context and compute is about 16-16.5 GiB (estimate), so Ollama probably offloads a few layers unless the projector stays off the GPU. The KB should qualify that line and point to `ollama ps` to check it. The llama.cpp recipe's own 15.2-15.7 GiB estimate was written against 15.81 GiB usable and should be rechecked against 15.47 GiB.
Gemma 4 31B: the exclusion is confirmed. The user's harness shows it is slowest even on a 614 GB/s Mac with everything in memory, and here it would offload 35-45% of a dense model to DDR5 (estimate).

Ollama tag identity: the KB's Ollama notes should state that the gemma4 default tags are multi-variant (GGUF for CUDA, MLX on Apple). The Mac's recorded disk sizes match the MLX variants, and the tags were republished in September-October 2026 after the user's August measurements. Mac pass/fail transfers as evidence about the model family and Studio loop, not as a byte-identical result for the GGUF a Linux host pulls.

Ollama version: the KB's Ollama notes are for v0.40.16, while the user's evidence is from 0.32.13/0.33.0 and shows the engine version can flip a cell from 5/5 to 1/5. If Ollama is used here to reproduce libredb results, pin an image tag (ollama/ollama:0.33.0 and 0.40.16 both exist on Docker Hub) and record it with the results.

Sampling: libredb drives every model at temperature 0 / top_p 1, while the KB recipes use the Gemma card's 1.0/0.95/top_k 64. The tool reliability shown in libredb was observed at greedy-ish sampling, so the KB should note that the OpenCode runs at card sampling are a different condition.

Speed transfer: the official Apple spec is 614 GB/s for the only M5 Max with 64 GB (40-core GPU) (https://www.apple.com/macbook-pro/specs/). For fully-in-VRAM Gemma sizes (e4b, 12b, 26b QAT via llama.cpp), this laptop's decode ceiling is about 1.46x the Mac's (estimate), and for offloaded ones (Ollama default 26b, 31b) it is lower. This could go in community-benchmarks.md as a transfer rule for the libredb numbers.
gaps: The libredb docs do not record the Ollama digest or runner (GGUF vs MLX) for the measured gemma4 tags, nor OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH/num_ctx, so it is unknown which quant and what context the Mac actually ran. The MLX inference rests only on matching disk sizes.

The gemma4 tags were republished after 22-23 August 2026 (today's manifests come from 2026-09-27/29 builds), so it is untested whether today's GGUF builds pass the same harness, and whether Ollama 0.33.0 can load the new manifests with draft layers.
Whether Ollama 0.40.x keeps the vision projector on the GPU for text-only requests is unverified, and that decides whether gemma4:26b-a4b-it-qat fits fully at 64k.
All fit and speed figures for this laptop are estimates. Nothing was run, because the GPU is busy and pulls are not allowed. DDR5 effective bandwidth (about 70-80 GB/s assumed) is unmeasured.

libredb tests short read-only SQL loops with small prompts. Long-context (64k+) behaviour, multi-line edit or write arguments, and streaming tool-call parsing, which matter for OpenCode, are not covered by this evidence.
measured-profiles.json says gemma4:e4b's assess cell re-read at 4/5 in a later sweep, which the published 30/30 does not show. The e4b result is marginal on that surface.
